source.title: List of unsolved problems in mathematics

accepted.question_text: Does the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture remain an unsolved Millennium Prize Problem?

evidence.quote:
Of the original seven Millennium Prize Problems listed by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000, six remain unsolved to date:[6]

    Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture

accepted.question_text: Does the Hodge conjecture remain an unsolved Millennium Prize Problem?

evidence.quote:
Of the original seven Millennium Prize Problems listed by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000, six remain unsolved to date:[6]

    Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
    Hodge conjecture

accepted.question_text: Does the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem remain an unsolved Millennium Prize Problem?

evidence.quote: Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness

accepted.question_text: Does the P versus NP problem remain an unsolved Millennium Prize Problem?

evidence.quote: P versus NP

accepted.question_text: Does the Riemann hypothesis remain an unsolved Millennium Prize Problem?

evidence.quote: Riemann hypothesis

accepted.question_text: Does the Yang–Mills existence and mass gap problem remain an unsolved Millennium Prize Problem?

evidence.quote: Yang–Mills existence and mass gap

accepted.question_text: Can a four-dimensional topological sphere have two or more inequivalent smooth structures?

evidence.quote:
However, a generalization
called the smooth four-dimensional Poincaré conjecture—that
is, whether a four-dimensional topological sphere can have
two or more inequivalent smooth structures—is unsolved.[13]

accepted.question_text: Is every finite lattice isomorphic to the congruence lattice of some finite algebra?

evidence.quote:
Finite lattice representation problem: is every finite lattice isomorphic to the congruence
lattice of some finite algebra?[21]

accepted.question_text: What is the largest possible determinant of a matrix whose entries are all equal to 1 or −1?

evidence.quote:
Hadamard's maximal determinant problem: what is the largest determinant of a matrix with
entries all equal to 1 or –1?

accepted.question_text: Do symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (SIC-POVMs) exist in all dimensions?

evidence.quote: Zauner's conjecture: do SIC-POVMs exist in all dimensions?

accepted.question_text: Does every bounded operator on a complex Banach space send some non-trivial closed subspace to itself?

evidence.quote:
Invariant subspace problem – does every bounded
operator on a complex Banach space send some non-
trivial closed subspace to itself?

accepted.question_text: Does every finite partially ordered set that is not totally ordered contain two elements x and y such that the probability that x appears before y in a random linear extension is between 1/3 and 2/3?

evidence.quote:
The 1/3–2/3 conjecture – does every finite partially ordered set that is not totally ordered
  contain two elements x and y such that the probability that x appears before y in a random
  linear extension is between 1/3 and 2/3?[29]

accepted.question_text: Is there an ergodic system with simple Lebesgue spectrum?

evidence.quote:
Banach's problem – is there an ergodic system with
simple Lebesgue spectrum?[36]

accepted.question_text: Is the Mandelbrot set locally connected?

evidence.quote: MLC conjecture – is the Mandelbrot set locally connected?

accepted.question_text: Does a regular compact contact type level set of a Hamiltonian on a symplectic manifold carry at least one periodic orbit of the Hamiltonian flow?

evidence.quote:
Weinstein conjecture – does a regular compact contact type level set of a Hamiltonian on a
symplectic manifold carry at least one periodic orbit of the Hamiltonian flow?

accepted.question_text: Is there a non-terminating game of beggar-my-neighbour?

evidence.quote: Is there a non-terminating game of beggar-my-neighbour?

accepted.question_text: How many Sudoku puzzles have exactly one solution?

evidence.quote:
Sudoku:

         How many puzzles have exactly one solution?[41]

accepted.question_text: Given the width of a tic-tac-toe board, what is the smallest dimension such that X is guaranteed to have a winning strategy?

evidence.quote:
Given the width of a tic-tac-toe board, what is the smallest dimension such that X is
guaranteed to have a winning strategy? (See also Hales-Jewett theorem)[42]

accepted.question_text: What is the outcome of a perfectly played game of chess?

evidence.quote:
What is the outcome of a perfectly played game of chess? (See also First-move
advantage in chess)

accepted.question_text: Do general elephants in algebraic geometry have at most Du Val singularities?

evidence.quote: General elephant problem: do general elephants have at most Du Val singularities?

accepted.question_text: If the union of finitely many axis-parallel squares has unit area, how small can the largest area covered by a disjoint subset of the squares be?

evidence.quote:
The covering problem of Rado: if the union of finitely many axis-parallel squares has unit
area, how small can the largest area covered by a disjoint subset of squares be?[46]

accepted.question_text: Can the classical isoperimetric inequality for subsets of Euclidean space be extended to spaces of nonpositive curvature known as Cartan–Hadamard manifolds?

evidence.quote:
Cartan–Hadamard conjecture: can the classical isoperimetric inequality for subsets of
Euclidean space be extended to spaces of nonpositive curvature, known as Cartan–
Hadamard manifolds?

accepted.question_text: What is the shortest route guaranteed to reach the boundary of a given shape when starting at an unknown point of the shape with unknown orientation?

evidence.quote:
Bellman's lost in a forest problem – find the shortest route that is guaranteed to reach the
boundary of a given shape, starting at an unknown point of the shape with unknown
orientation[66]

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a two-dimensional shape that is a prototile for an aperiodic tiling but not for any periodic tiling?

evidence.quote:
The einstein problem – does there exist a two-dimensional shape that forms the prototile for
an aperiodic tiling, but not for any periodic tiling?[70][a]

accepted.question_text: Does every Jordan curve have an inscribed square?

evidence.quote:
Inscribed square problem, also known as Toeplitz' conjecture and the square peg problem –
does every Jordan curve have an inscribed square?[73]

accepted.question_text: What is the smallest area of a plane shape that can cover every unit-length curve in the plane?

evidence.quote:
Moser's worm problem – what is the smallest area of a shape that can cover every unit-
length curve in the plane?[78]

accepted.question_text: What is the largest area of a shape that can be maneuvered through a unit-width L-shaped corridor?

evidence.quote:
The moving sofa problem – what is the largest area of a shape that can be maneuvered
through a unit-width L-shaped corridor?[79]

accepted.question_text: Does every convex polyhedron have Rupert’s property?

evidence.quote: Does every convex polyhedron have Rupert's property?[80][81]

accepted.question_text: Does every convex polyhedron have a net, or simple edge-unfolding?

evidence.quote:
Shephard's problem (a.k.a. Dürer's conjecture) – does every convex polyhedron have a net,
or simple edge-unfolding?[82][83]

accepted.question_text: What is the minimum-energy configuration of mutually repelling particles on a unit sphere?

evidence.quote:
The Thomson problem – what is the minimum energy configuration of mutually-repelling
particles on a unit sphere?[84]

accepted.question_text: What is the maximum chromatic number of biplanar graphs?

evidence.quote:
The Earth–Moon problem: what is the maximum
chromatic number of biplanar graphs?[87]

accepted.question_text: Is there a drawing of any complete bipartite graph with fewer crossings than the number given by Zarankiewicz?

evidence.quote:
Turán's brick factory problem – Is there a drawing of any complete bipartite graph with fewer
crossings than the number given by Zarankiewicz?[100]

accepted.question_text: Are there graphs on n vertices whose word representation requires more than floor(n/2) copies of each letter?

evidence.quote:
Are there any graphs on n vertices whose representation requires more than floor(n/2)
copies of each letter?[109][110][111][112]

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a strongly regular graph with parameters (99,14,1,2)?

evidence.quote:
Conway's 99-graph problem: does there exist a strongly regular graph with parameters
(99,14,1,2)?[116]

accepted.question_text: Does a Moore graph with girth 5 and degree 57 exist?

evidence.quote: Does a Moore graph with girth 5 and degree 57 exist?[123]

accepted.question_text: Does every oriented graph contain a vertex for which there are at least as many other vertices at distance two as at distance one?

evidence.quote:
The second neighborhood problem: does every oriented graph contain a vertex for which
there are at least as many other vertices at distance two as at distance one?[127]

accepted.question_text: How many edges can there be in a bipartite graph on a given number of vertices with no complete bipartite subgraphs of a given size?

evidence.quote:
Zarankiewicz problem: how many edges can there be in a bipartite graph on a given number
of vertices with no complete bipartite subgraphs of a given size?

accepted.question_text: For which positive integers m and n is the free Burnside group B(m,n) finite, and in particular is B(2,5) finite?

evidence.quote:
For which positive integers m, n is the free Burnside group B(m,n) finite? In particular, is
B(2, 5) finite?

accepted.question_text: For which number fields does Hilbert’s tenth problem hold?

evidence.quote: For which number fields does Hilbert's tenth problem hold?

accepted.question_text: Is the theory of the real numbers with the exponential function decidable?

evidence.quote:
Tarski's exponential function problem: is the theory of the real numbers with the exponential
function decidable?

accepted.question_text: Is every infinite minimal field of characteristic zero algebraically closed, where minimal means every definable subset of the structure is finite or co-finite?

evidence.quote:
Is every infinite, minimal field of characteristic zero algebraically closed? (Here, "minimal"
means that every definable subset of the structure is finite or co-finite.)

accepted.question_text: Is every irreducible component of the Zariski closure of a set of special points in a Shimura variety a special subvariety?

evidence.quote:
André–Oort conjecture: is every irreducible component of the Zariski closure of a set of
special points in a Shimura variety a special subvariety?

accepted.question_text: Is there a dense set of points in the plane all at rational distances from one another?

evidence.quote:
Erdős–Ulam problem: is there a dense set of points in the plane all at rational distances from
one-another?

accepted.question_text: How far can the number of integer points in a circle centered at the origin be from the area of the circle?

evidence.quote:
The Gauss circle problem: how far can the number of integer points in a circle centered at
the origin be from the area of the circle?

accepted.question_text: Do the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line?

evidence.quote:
Riemann hypothesis: do the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the
critical line     with real ?

accepted.question_text: Are there infinitely many perfect numbers?

evidence.quote: Are there infinitely many perfect numbers?

accepted.question_text: Do any odd perfect numbers exist?

evidence.quote: Do any odd perfect numbers exist?

accepted.question_text: Can a 3×3 magic square be constructed from 9 distinct perfect square numbers?

evidence.quote: Can a 3×3 magic square be constructed from 9 distinct perfect square numbers?[153]

accepted.question_text: Can integer factorization be done in polynomial time?

evidence.quote: Can integer factorization be done in polynomial time?

accepted.question_text: Are there infinitely many twin primes?

evidence.quote: Twin prime conjecture: there are infinitely many twin primes.

accepted.question_text: Are there infinitely many Mersenne primes, equivalently infinitely many even perfect numbers?

evidence.quote:
Are there infinitely many Mersenne primes (Lenstra–Pomerance–Wagstaff conjecture);
equivalently, infinitely many even perfect numbers?

accepted.question_text: Does the generalized continuum hypothesis below a strongly compact cardinal imply the generalized continuum hypothesis everywhere?

evidence.quote:
(Woodin) Does the generalized continuum hypothesis below a strongly compact cardinal
imply the generalized continuum hypothesis everywhere?

accepted.question_text: Without assuming the axiom of choice, can a nontrivial elementary embedding V→V exist?

evidence.quote: Without assuming the axiom of choice, can a nontrivial elementary embedding V→V exist?

accepted.question_text: Can unknots be recognized in polynomial time?

evidence.quote: Unknotting problem: can unknots be recognized in polynomial time?
